data.intent: Founder-activated Level 3 Quality War: turn Module 2 'Money in Motion' into an extraordinary complete three-lesson module. Architecture war first (Candidates A/B/C with played prototypes), then vertical build, then independent gates, ending in a founder ship case. Box Office is Candidate A, not the presumptive winner.

contract.hypothesis: Module 2 'Money in Motion' can become a coherent three-lesson sports-business module in which (1) the winning architecture is selected from genuinely competing candidates (A: evolve The Box Office; B: substantial refound preserving its verified insights; C: first-principles, sunk-cost-blind) via played browser prototypes, not prose comparison; (2) every flagship lesson rates STRONG or MAGNETIC on independent gameplay review; (3) every taught mechanism is economically true and instantiated in play before it is named; (4) real NBA/sports-business people, contracts, rules, and events are integral, dated, and never a fandom test; (5) a fresh-context teacher review finds each lesson runnable to an excellent standard without founder knowledge; and (6) the runtime survives classroom behavior on the three surfaces.
contract.whyThisMatters: Module 2 is the first module built under Economics Boss and the second module of Track 101. The existing Box Office prototype is technically verified but has never been gameplay/economics/teacher-gauntleted, and its architecture has never faced a competitor. Committing three lessons of build effort to an unexamined architecture is the exact sunk-cost failure the product philosophy forbids.
uncertainties: Whether the Price Dial / hidden-demand-curve discovery loop is STRONG when actually played, or merely FUNCTIONAL.
What the correct three-lesson economic arc for 'money in motion' is (revenue/price/demand -> ? -> ?), and whether revenue sharing and league institutions belong in it.
Whether real historical sports-business situations (commit-then-reveal) beat operated-simulation lessons for one or more slots.
Whether class interdependence (shared markets, competing prices) materially improves the economics or adds multiplayer cost without teaching value.
Whether a random competent teacher can run a reveal-heavy economics lesson without founder knowledge.
Whether Boss's workstream-lead machinery actually helps on a real product program (first live test).
requiredEvidence: Three genuinely independent candidate module architectures on file, each with per-lesson fantasy/verb/system/mechanism/real-sports/consequence/classroom/reveal/teacher/synthesis definitions.

Played browser prototypes (browser-trace) for the uncertain signature loops of at least two competing candidates, with played-strategy notes (optimizing, random, cautious, aggressive, minimal-reading, replay).
A dated sports-reality-report delivered before architecture selection, proposing real sports-business material as design input.
An economic-truth-report covering mechanism truth, dominant strategies, false-lesson risk, and the full synthesis map for the winning architecture.
gameplay-report per flagship lesson from an independent critic who played the browser build, rating STRONG or better.
A fresh-context teacher-transfer-report (teacher-facing material first, builder context withheld) per lesson.
projector-report treating the three surfaces as one session, including board privacy verification.
visual-report against the premium sports-business media bar on rendered browser output.
Passing test evidence recorded via evidence command (full runtime suite), plus rerunnable e2e proofs for each lesson arc.
analyst-report attempting to disprove the program's claims against the recorded evidence.
nonGoals: Reopening or polishing Module 1 beyond narrow shared-runtime fixes a Module 2 regression forces.
World selectors, motif systems, commerce, enterprise, or Decision Challenges integration.
Extracting a generic economics engine or generalizing the Boss harness.
Redesigning or reinstalling the Boss harness itself.
sacredConstraints: Standing decisions D1-D19 hold; no silent mutation of the decision log.
Four-module spine fixed (D1/D2); Module 2 stays 'Money in Motion' in the M2 slot.
No XP/levels/badges/leaderboards (D4): the class reveal is the reward system.
Real-world sports business is mandatory product direction; sports knowledge may never be a prerequisite for the economics; reality never becomes a fandom test.
Simplify the interface before simplifying the economics; material simplifications are recorded with misconception risk.
boardView is structurally never handed a seat identity; /teach stays behind the per-session bearer key (D14).
Every synchronized reveal ships a manual teacher fallback.
Each module owns its state behind the LessonModule contract; no premature generic engine.
A fun simulation that teaches false economics fails.
Fictional student names only on shared screens.
The founder controls merge to main; no auto-merge.
contract.passCondition: All three lessons of the selected architecture are built, integrated, and independently verified: gameplay STRONG+ per flagship from played browser evidence; economic-truth report with zero unresolved blocking findings and a complete synthesis map; dated sports-reality report with no unresolved factual blockers; fresh-context teacher-transfer report finding no hidden-founder-knowledge blockers; projector/board privacy verified; full test suite and per-lesson e2e proofs green via evidence command; analyst reconciliation confirms the claims; ship case prepared for founder merge decision.
contract.repairCondition: The selected architecture holds under independent review but named findings (gameplay below STRONG on a flagship, a repairable economic-truth defect, a teacher-transfer gap, a runtime defect) remain within the repair budget and each has a bounded, evidence-backed repair path.
contract.rollbackCondition: Integrated Module 2 work measurably degrades the shared runtime or Module 1's verified behavior (test or e2e regressions attributable to this program) and the degradation cannot be repaired within budget: revert to the recorded checkpoint.
contract.killCondition: Independent play evidence shows the selected architecture's signature loop is WEAK/REFOUND at its core (not repairable by tuning), or the economics it teaches is false at the mechanism level, or no candidate architecture produces a flagship above FUNCTIONAL after the prototype war: kill or refound the module architecture rather than shipping it.

iterationBudget.reason: Level 3 quality war on a flagship module: one architecture-war wave with competing prototypes, one selection/vertical-build wave per lesson tier, independent gate waves, and bounded repairs. Token measurement unavailable in this harness; waves are the binding budget.

data.label: Sports Reality design input: 15 dated real-world anchors + ranked top-5 for Module 2

sections.real-world-anchors: 15 verified, dated anchors in docs/gauntlet/module-2/SPORTS_REALITY_INPUT.md covering ticket/gate pricing, the 2024 $76B/11-yr Disney-NBC-Amazon media deal and its cap effects (+10% to $154.647M for 2025-26, +6.7% to $164.961M for 2026-27), NBA revenue sharing and market-size gaps (Warriors $833M revenue vs Grizzlies sub-$10M local-TV era), luxury tax/second apron as incentive design (2025 Celtics champion teardown, ~$456M league tax 2024-25), relocation/expansion economics (2013 Kings-to-Seattle owners' vote 22-8, $534M Sacramento sale; 2026 expansion watch), player-driven revenue shocks (Caitlin Clark: Fever 4,066->17,036 attendance, $250M expansion fees, March 2026 CBA cap $1.5M->$7M), Green Bay's published books ($453.2M national share per team, July 2026) as the one earned cross-league exception, plus Suns free-TV gamble and Luka-trade fan-goodwill reserves.
sections.accuracy-findings: Every factual claim carries verifiedAsOf dates and sources; post-Jan-2026 facts web-verified. Modeled demand curves must never present invented team-specific numbers as fact — flagged to Economic Truth.
sections.staleness-findings: Cap/tax figures age every June; NBA expansion could resolve any month (Silver: determination due end of 2026). All product copy needs season stamps.
sections.rights-source-considerations: Names, facts, and statistics only; no anchor requires logos, photos, video, likenesses, or proprietary datasets. No blanket legal claims made.
sections.recommendation: Highest-severity finding: Box Office's fictional Market Cards and generic TV pipe are exactly where reality is materially stronger at identical build cost — replace with Knicks/Thunder/Warriors/Grizzlies and the real national media deal. Ranked top-5 anchors map to lesson-shaped opportunities: (1) real-market ticket pricing, (2) Caitlin Clark demand shock, (3) Kings-to-Seattle commit-then-reveal + Seattle/Milwaukee arena-subsidy pair (outcome != decision quality), (4) second-apron incentive design, (5) Green Bay open books for revenue sharing.

data.label: Module 2 economic learning contract: concept verdicts, false-lesson risks, dominant-strategy analysis incl. existing Box Office model, three candidate arcs, R1-R16

data.finding: The existing Box Office demand model must not carry into the selected architecture unrepaired: (1) pre-lock server preview returns true attendance/revenue for every dial position, so the optimum is read by sweeping, not reasoned — the hidden-curve uncertainty is fake; (2) computed over the full price grid, sweet-spot pricing is optimal in both homestands for all four markets — the claimed short-term-cash-vs-fan-base tension does not exist; (3) an overpriced Expansion seat faces a $75,000 H2 payroll against a $52,500 revenue ceiling — unwinnable by construction. See ECONOMIC_CONTRACT.md R2/R5/R6/R10.

sections.mechanism-verdicts: Revenue-as-hump is a 5-minute discovery, not a lesson; it must pair with demand shifters or it teaches a falsehood. The deep unowned M2 concepts are joint product/externality, revenue sharing with moral hazard, and incentives/institution design. Segmentation repeats M1's allocation verb; sunk cost belongs to M1 L2. Every concept must pass two tests: delete it and the numbers change (instantiation), and a sweep/copy cannot reach the optimum (reasoning). Full verdicts in docs/gauntlet/module-2/ECONOMIC_CONTRACT.md.
sections.false-lesson-risks: Two biggest: 'revenue maximization is the franchise's goal' (prevented only by two non-collapsible scoreboards from lesson 1) and 'charging high is greedy, charging low is kind' (prevented by symmetric error penalties). Also live: price fully controls attendance; sharing is charity; the real team was right because it happened; small markets fail because they're badly run.
sections.dominant-strategies: In the existing Box Office model: the pre-lock preview serves true attendance/revenue for every dial position (boxOffice.ts:374), so the optimum is read, not reasoned, and REVEAL restates a known number; computed over the full price grid, sweet-spot pricing is optimal in both homestands for all four markets — the claimed short-term-cash-vs-fan-base tension does not exist; an overpriced Expansion seat faces a $75,000 H2 bill against a $52,500 revenue ceiling (unwinnable by construction). Generic traps: free-riding and vote-my-assignment in sharing games; headcount dominance and guess-the-teacher's-answer in rule design; guess-what-happened in historical reveals.
sections.synthesis-map-verdict: Bet on Arc A 'The Flow': my money loop -> other people are in my loop -> we write the rule. Ordering forced at every seam; covers D2's named concepts without trespassing on M3/M4; uses class interdependence only where the economics requires it. Arcs B (Ticket Window) and C (Owner's Problem) specified and rejected with reasons; C's two-scoreboard structure transplanted into A as mandatory. Full synthesis chains per lesson in the doc.
sections.required-repairs: R1-R16, falsifiable, in the doc. Hardest: L3 must get from vote to played consequence in ~20 minutes or it is a debate club. Formal dissent recorded against carrying the Box Office model forward unrepaired on R2/R5/R6/R10.
